IA01.why: Same 'equation has no solution' constant condition (equal coefficients, different constants), but here it is only the first step; b is then used in a second equation with a given solution. Format is common on official SAT (no-solution constants).
Second half (k(x - c) = ... with a given solution x, find c) is SAT-060's template; the no-solution step is new.

IC01.why: Same 'random assignment experiment, which conclusion' format; issue here is confounding (greenhouse), not scope. Also retired SAT-222 format; not its template.

IA02.why: Identity-in-x condition (true for every s) as in 013/273, but derived from two score procedures; reasoning similar, setup differs.

IC04.why: Same template: data with given mean and SD undergo a linear transformation; report new mean and SD from a 2x2 choice grid. 50 - x (slope -1) vs 3x + 5; reasoning identical (mean transforms, SD scales by |a|, shift ignored). Textbook classic.

IA06.why: Contextual version of SAT-271: a lower bound and an upper bound on y, ask the greatest x; max x is the intersection of the two boundary lines (here (12, 6)). Same setup and asked quantity once translated.
Greatest amount of one item in a two-constraint contextual inequality system (one max, one min); CA05 combines via substitution, same skill/ask.

IC06.why: Drops-to-volume unit conversion over time; different direction and ask. Textbook classic (nursing IV drip-rate formula).

IA07.why: Two-tier pricing inverted to find usage (596 inverts via average cost); here a doubled bill. Also ACT-758 computes one tiered bill (first step here).

IC07.why: Margin-of-error interval from a random sample; adds a self-selected comparison. Also SAT-637/ACT-205 bias themes. Resembles official SAT self-selected-vs-random items.

IA08.why: Interpret a constant in a rewritten linear cost model; different form (factored constant), not a template.

IC09.why: Same two-stage setup (container chosen with probability 1/2, then an item at random); IC09 runs it in reverse (Bayes: P(room B | senior)), whose first step is ACT-468's total probability. Borderline template under the 'reverse setup' rule. Classic Bayes urn problem; beyond typical SAT conditional-probability (two-way table) scope.

IC10.why: Two groups combined, which must be true of a statistic of the combined data (median in 312, SD here); different statistic and reasoning.

IA12.why: Final step is exactly the retired 'score needed on 4th test for target mean' template ((234 + x)/4 >= 82); the weighted-grade step is added in front. Demo fixture (sixth score for mean 86) is the same final step.

IC12.why: Same setup (revenue split by share, one part +x%, the other -y%); 131 asks the new share, IC12 asks the total change, which is an intermediate step of 131. Also SAT-606.

IA13.why: Same 2x2 template: two products each containing two components in fixed amounts, exact totals of both components given, find the amount of one product (recipes eggs/milk vs fertilizer nitrogen/phosphorus, percent coefficients). Also ideas-gen-04 N08 (source of 377). Textbook classic two-nutrient blend.

IC13.why: Aspect ratio plus a second measurement to recover dimensions (544: ratio + diagonal -> area; here ratio + area -> width).

IA14.why: Least amount for which plan B is at least as good as plan A (two-plan break-even); the commission threshold changes the setup, so only close. ACT-757 supplies the threshold-commission piece.

IC14.why: Same 'what happens to mean and median' choice set (mean decreases, median unchanged is the key in both); mechanism differs (corrected max vs added values at the median). Also ACT-168, SAT-185.
